documents.title: General Surgery Discharge Summary
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Admission 12/30/2024 - Discharge 01/07/2025
Service: General Surgery

Dx: recurrent adhesive small-bowel obstruction; postoperative urinary retention; catheter-related urethral injury
Procedure: exploratory laparotomy with lysis of adhesions 12/31/2024 (no bowel resection)

Course: Readmitted four weeks after nonoperative management of an adhesive SBO with return of colicky pain, emesis and obstipation; imaging again showed small-bowel obstruction. Given recurrence, taken to the OR 12/31 for laparotomy and adhesiolysis; all bowel viable. Diet advanced from POD 2 and tolerated, bowel function returned POD 3.
Urethral catheter removed morning of 1/3. He did not void and bladder scan showed retention; straight catheterization done. On 1/4 an indwelling catheter could not be passed beyond the proximal urethra and there was blood at the meatus - see urology consult. Catheter placed by urology over a wire; to remain about three weeks.

Discharge meds: amlodipine 5 mg daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily, acetaminophen 1 g every 6 h as needed.
Allergies: NKDA
Wound: midline staples in place, clean. Staples out at surgery clinic in about 2 weeks. No lifting over 10 lb for 6 weeks.
Catheter: leg bag by day, night bag at night. Urology clinic in about 3 weeks for catheter study.
Follow-up: PCP 1 week.

documents.title: Urology Inpatient Consultation
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
UROLOGY CONSULT - 01/04/2025
Reason: difficult catheter placement, blood at meatus

67-year-old with BPH on tamsulosin, POD 4 from laparotomy and adhesiolysis for a recurrent adhesive obstruction (first admitted for obstruction in late November). Retained after his catheter came out yesterday. This morning nursing tried to re-site a catheter; it stopped after a few centimeters, he had a sudden pain in the perineum, and some blood showed at the tip of the penis. Catheter pulled back at once and we were called.

Meds: amlodipine, lisinopril, tamsulosin. NKDA.
FH: father HTN/CAD, mother diverticular disease. Former smoker, 15 pk-yr. Retired math teacher.

Exam: palpable, distended bladder above the pubis. Perineum mildly tender to touch, no swelling, no scrotal hematoma. Small amount of dried blood at meatus.

Retrograde urethrogram (performed today): extravasation of contrast at the bulbar urethra with contrast also continuing into the bladder - partial bulbar urethral disruption. Posterior urethra and bladder neck otherwise unremarkable.

Assessment: iatrogenic partial bulbar urethral injury; urinary retention after surgery in a man with BPH.

Plan: flexible cystoscopy at bedside; guidewire passed through the injured segment into the bladder and a 16 Fr catheter railroaded over it without difficulty, clear urine after initial blood-tinged drainage. Keep catheter about 3 weeks, then pericatheter urethrogram in clinic. Continue tamsulosin. Nobody else to manipulate the catheter - call urology for any problem.

documents.title: Post-discharge Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 6 days after discharge. Second SBO admission - this time went to the OR 12/31 for laparotomy and adhesiolysis, no resection. Course complicated by retention after the catheter came out and then a partial bulbar urethral tear during a re-catheterization attempt 1/4; urology placed a catheter over a wire. Op note, discharge summary and urology consult all reviewed.

Today: incision a little sore, using acetaminophen once or twice a day. Eating normally, BMs daily. Catheter draining yellow urine, some perineal ache that is improving. No fevers. Managing the leg bag fine though says he 'is counting the days.'

Meds reviewed: amlodipine 5, lisinopril 10, tamsulosin 0.4, acetaminophen prn. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted, afebrile. Midline incision with staples, edges together, no erythema or drainage. Abdomen soft, appropriately tender near incision. Catheter in place, urine clear. No calf tenderness.

A/P
1. S/p laparotomy/adhesiolysis for recurrent adhesive SBO - healing. Staples at surgery clinic next week.
2. Partial bulbar urethral injury, catheter in - urology follow-up ~1/24 for the dye study. Catheter care reviewed.
3. Urinary retention post-op, BPH - continue tamsulosin.
4. HTN - fine.
I'll check in by text next week.

documents.title: General Surgery Clinic Letter
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

I saw your patient today three weeks out from laparotomy and adhesiolysis. He is eating a full diet with regular bowel movements and only minor incisional discomfort. The midline wound has healed; staples were removed and adhesive strips applied. No hernia on cough.

No lifting over 10 lb until six weeks after surgery, then no restriction. He knows adhesions can recur and what symptoms should bring him in. No routine follow-up needed with us.

Meds as listed by your office. NKDA.

General Surgery

documents.title: Urology Clinic Note
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
UROLOGY - 01/24/2025

Returns 20 days after cystoscopic catheter placement for a partial bulbar urethral injury sustained during catheterization after abdominal surgery.

Pericatheter urethrogram: contrast outlines a smooth bulbar urethra with no extravasation. Catheter removed. Bladder filled by gravity and he voided in clinic; post-void residual by bladder scan 150 mL.

Impression: urethral injury healed. Voiding with a modest residual on a background of BPH.

Plan: continue tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily. Watch for slowing of the stream or spraying that could mean a stricture forming. Recheck flow and residual in 3 months.

Meds: amlodipine 5 mg, lisinopril 10 mg, tamsulosin 0.4 mg. NKDA.

Urology

documents.title: Refills
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good morning. My blood pressure pills and the prostate one are on their last refill from the old doctor. Can you send new ones to the same pharmacy? Also the catheter is out and I am a new man.

documents.title: RE: Refills
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Great news about the catheter. Sent amlodipine, lisinopril and tamsulosin, 90 days with refills. See you in March.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
BP f/u. Feeling back to normal after the winter of hospitals. Walking 2 miles again. Bowels regular. Urine stream 'about what it was' before all this, up once a night. No dysuria.
Home BP readings run 128-138 / 78-84.
Meds: amlodipine 5, lisinopril 10, tamsulosin 0.4. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Midline scar healed, no bulge. No edema.

A/P
HTN - at goal, continue both. BMP today.
BPH / recent retention - urology recheck next month.
S/p adhesiolysis - doing well.
RTC June.

documents.title: Urology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Thank you for sharing the care of this 67-year-old with BPH and a healed bulbar urethral injury from January.

He reports a weaker stream than before the winter and a sense of not emptying fully; nocturia once. No dysuria, no hematuria, no spraying.

Exam: prostate smooth, symmetric, nontender, about 50 g. Post-void residual by bladder scan 240 mL.

Impression: chronic urinary retention from benign prostatic obstruction. No sign of urethral stricture.

Plan: continue tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily. We talked through an outlet procedure; he would like to hold off for now, which is reasonable. Recheck in 6 months, sooner for infection or inability to void.

Urology

documents.title: No-show
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt did not arrive for 10:30. Left VM. He called back at 2 pm, had the date wrong in his calendar. Offered video next week, accepted.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, pt at his kitchen table, ID verified.
Apologized for missing last week. Doing well. Sent a photo of his BP log - two weeks of mornings, mostly 126-136/76-84, one 142/86 after a bad night's sleep.
No dizziness, no ankle swelling. Saw urology in April: residual a bit high, staying on tamsulosin, he's not keen on a procedure yet.
Meds unchanged. NKDA.

A/P
HTN controlled - continue amlodipine 5 / lisinopril 10.
BPH with retention - per urology, recheck there in the fall. Told him to call if he can't go, gets fevers or burning.
Wellness visit and labs in September.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL WELLNESS VISIT - turns 68 today.

Interval: no hospital visits since January. Urology in April: residual 240, chronic retention from the prostate, continuing tamsulosin, procedure deferred by his choice. Says the stream is slow and he sometimes goes back to the bathroom a second time. No UTIs, no fevers.
HTN: home readings in the low-mid 130s/80s.
Bowels regular since surgery, no pain or bloating.

Functional: independent with everything, drives, does his own finances and the yard. No falls. Hearing fine for conversation. Vision corrected, eye exam last year.
Cognition: clock and 3-word recall normal.
Mood: PHQ-2 0.
Safety: seat belt, smoke detectors, no firearms.
Habits: ex-smoker, 15 pk-yr. A drink or so a month. Walks most days.

Meds: amlodipine 5, lisinopril 10, tamsulosin 0.4. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, healed midline and subcostal scars, no hernia. No edema.

Prevention:
- Colonoscopy 2019, diverticulosis only, next 2029.
- Lung screening: not eligible at 15 pk-yr.
- AAA: aorta normal caliber on CT 11/2024, satisfies screening.
- Vaccines: PCV20 2024, Shingrix done, Tdap 2017. Flu/COVID due next month - nurse visit booked.
- Hep C / HIV done 2024.

Plan: CBC, CMP, lipids today. Written prevention schedule given. Follow BP 3-4 mo. Urology recheck this fall.

documents.title: Wellness visit labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Walter, labs are all normal - kidneys, salts, blood count, cholesterol. No changes. Nurse visit for your shots is on the books for 10/7.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Screening questions negative, no prior reactions. High-dose flu given IM in the left arm, 2025-26 COVID (Moderna) IM in the right arm. Observed 15 min, no reaction. Mentioned he has a urology ultrasound next week.

reports.text:
INDICATION: Chronic urinary retention, BPH.
COMPARISON: CT abdomen/pelvis 11/2024.
FINDINGS: Right kidney 11.0 cm, left kidney 11.3 cm, normal cortical thickness and echogenicity. No hydronephrosis, stones or masses in either kidney. Bladder: pre-void volume 470 mL; a single mobile echogenic focus with posterior shadowing in the dependent bladder measuring 1.6 cm, consistent with a calculus. Post-void residual 310 mL. Prostate volume 52 mL.
reports.conclusion: 1.6 cm bladder stone. Post-void residual 310 mL. Prostate 52 mL. Normal kidneys without hydronephrosis.

documents.title: Urology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Dear Doctor,

Your patient's follow-up ultrasound shows a 1.6 cm bladder stone, a post-void residual of 310 mL and a 52 mL prostate; the kidneys are normal without hydronephrosis. The stone is almost certainly a product of incomplete emptying.

We have scheduled cystoscopy with laser cystolitholapaxy at our surgery center for 11/26. He again prefers to stay on tamsulosin rather than add an outlet procedure at the same sitting; we will revisit that afterward. Please send a preoperative history and physical with an ECG and basic labs.

Urology

reports.text: Sinus rhythm, rate 72. PR 170 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc 418 ms. Normal axis. No ST or T wave abnormality. No prior for comparison.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Preoperative Evaluation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
PRE-OP H&P
Procedure: cystoscopy with laser cystolitholapaxy, 11/26, urology surgery center, general or spinal anesthesia.
Indication: 1.6 cm bladder stone with chronic retention from BPH (PVR 310 on 10/14 US).

Hx: HTN, BPH with chronic retention, diverticulosis. Laparotomy/adhesiolysis 12/2024 under general without anesthetic problems; partial bulbar urethral injury 1/2025, healed. Remote open cholecystectomy.
Functional capacity: walks 2 miles, climbs 2 flights without stopping - well over 4 METs.
No CP, SOB, palpitations, syncope. No bleeding history. No anticoagulants or antiplatelets.
Meds: amlodipine 5, lisinopril 10, tamsulosin 0.4. NKDA.
Former smoker, rare alcohol.

Exam: vitals as charted. Airway unremarkable. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, healed scars. No edema.
ECG: normal sinus rhythm, no ST-T changes.
Labs: CBC, BMP drawn - will forward.

Assessment: low-risk procedure, good functional capacity, no active cardiac conditions. Acceptable risk; no further testing needed.
Recs: take amlodipine and tamsulosin morning of surgery; hold lisinopril the morning of. Resume after.
Faxed to urology with labs when back.

documents.title: Pre-op packet sent
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pre-op H&P, ECG tracing and labs (CBC, BMP normal) faxed to urology surgery center. Confirmation page received.

documents.title: Operative Note - Cystolitholapaxy
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Date: 11/26/2025
Procedure: cystourethroscopy with holmium laser cystolitholapaxy
Anesthesia: general (LMA)
Preop antibiotic: single IV dose per protocol

Findings: anterior urethra normal caliber, bulbar segment patent and well healed at the site of the January injury. Prostatic urethra with enlarged lateral lobes. Single 1.6 cm bladder stone, fragmented and evacuated completely. Ureteral orifices normal. No bladder tumor.

No complications. Catheter not left. Voided before discharge home the same day.
Plan: continue tamsulosin. Urology clinic in the spring to recheck residual and discuss outlet surgery again.

Urology

reports.text:
INDICATION: Fever, new murmur, positive blood cultures.
FINDINGS: Normal left ventricular size and wall thickness; LVEF estimated 60%. Normal right ventricular size and function. A mobile echodensity is attached to the tricuspid valve. Aortic, mitral and pulmonic valves appear structurally normal without vegetation. No pericardial effusion. IVC normal with respiratory variation.
reports.conclusion: Mobile mass on the tricuspid valve, consistent with vegetation in this setting. Normal biventricular function.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of visit: 12/12/2025

CC: fevers on and off for nearly a week

HPI: 68M, HTN, BPH with chronic retention, diverticulosis; hospitalized last winter for adhesive SBO needing laparotomy, complicated by a catheter-related urethral injury. Had cystoscopy with bladder stone removal about two weeks ago. Since roughly 12/6 has had intermittent fevers, feeling run down, and not wanting to eat. No cough, no dysuria, no abdominal pain.
No prosthetic valves, no indwelling lines. Never used IV drugs.
Meds: amlodipine 5, lisinopril 10, tamsulosin 0.4. NKDA.
FH: father HTN/CAD; mother diverticular disease.

Triage temp 38.3 C (101 F).

Exam: febrile, tired-appearing. New holosystolic murmur loudest at the left lower sternal border. No Janeway lesions, no Osler nodes. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign. No CVA tenderness.

Workup: three blood culture sets from separate sites drawn before antibiotics. All three flagged positive overnight with gram-positive cocci in pairs and chains; identified as an Enterococcus species, later E. faecalis. TTE: mobile mass on the tricuspid valve.

Impression: enterococcal infective endocarditis of the tricuspid valve, likely seeded from the recent urologic procedure.
Plan: admit to medicine, ID and cardiology consults, empiric therapy after cultures.

medications.sig: 2 g IV every 4 hours via PICC through 1/25/2026
2 g IV every 12 hours via PICC through 1/25/2026

results.text: Set 1 of 2: no growth at 5 days.
Set 2 of 2: no growth at 5 days.

documents.title: Hospital Medicine Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Admission 12/12/2025 - Discharge 12/19/2025

Principal dx: native tricuspid valve infective endocarditis, Enterococcus faecalis (ampicillin-susceptible)
Other: HTN, BPH with chronic urinary retention, diverticulosis

Course: Admitted from ED with fever, new murmur, 3 of 3 blood culture sets positive and a tricuspid mass on TTE. Recent cystoscopy with stone removal (11/26) the likely portal. Started on ampicillin plus ceftriaxone after ID input once the isolate was identified. Fever resolved within 48 h. Repeat cultures 12/14 no growth - that date counts as day 1 of therapy.
TEE 12/15: 1.1 cm mobile vegetation on the tricuspid valve. No perivalvular abscess. Aortic, mitral and pulmonic valves normal. Cardiology: no surgical indication; medical therapy.
PICC placed right arm 12/17, tip at cavoatrial junction.
Appetite returning at discharge, ambulating independently.

Discharge meds:
- ampicillin 2 g IV q4h (home infusion pump) through 1/25/2026
- ceftriaxone 2 g IV q12h through 1/25/2026
- amlodipine 5 mg daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily - unchanged
Allergies: NKDA

Follow-up: home infusion with weekly CBC and BMP to ID and PCP. ID clinic at end of therapy. Repeat TTE after therapy. PCP within 1 week.

documents.title: Infectious Diseases Consultation
documents.author: infectious diseases
documents.body:
ID CONSULT - 12/13/2025

68-year-old man with BPH and chronic retention who had cystoscopic stone removal 11/26, now with a week of fevers, a new tricuspid-area murmur, 3/3 cultures with E. faecalis (ampicillin-susceptible) and a tricuspid vegetation on TTE. No IV drug use, no prosthetic material or lines. Genitourinary source most likely.

Recommendations:
1. Ampicillin 2 g IV q4h plus ceftriaxone 2 g IV q12h - avoids aminoglycoside toxicity at his age.
2. Repeat blood cultures until negative; duration 6 weeks from the first negative set.
3. TEE to define the vegetation and look for abscess.
4. PICC once cultures clear; OPAT with weekly CBC and BMP.
5. ID clinic near end of therapy.

Infectious Diseases

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called after hospital records came in. Home since Friday. Infusion nurse came Saturday and set him up; ampicillin runs on a pump, he does the ceftriaxone twice a day himself after teaching. PICC dressing dry. No fevers since discharge, temps 98s. Eating better. Knows to call for fever, arm swelling or redness at the line. TCM visit 12/29 confirmed.

documents.title: Home Infusion Weekly Labs
documents.author: home infusion pharmacy
documents.body: OPAT weekly monitoring, week 2 of therapy. Draw 12/26 via PICC. CBC with diff and BMP attached. Line flushing well, dressing changed, site clean. Doses on schedule, no missed infusions. Copy to ID.

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-discharge visit. Admitted 12/12-12/19 with E. faecalis tricuspid valve endocarditis, 2 weeks after his cystolitholapaxy. TEE 1.1 cm vegetation, no abscess, no surgery needed. On ampicillin + ceftriaxone via R arm PICC until 1/25. Records, ID consult and first OPAT labs reviewed.

He's tired but better each day. No fevers at home. Appetite back. Pump is a nuisance at night. Voiding ok, no burning. No SOB, no leg swelling.

Meds: ampicillin 2 g IV q4h, ceftriaxone 2 g IV q12h, amlodipine 5, lisinopril 10, tamsulosin 0.4. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted, afebrile. Systolic murmur at LLSB. Lungs clear. PICC site R upper arm clean, no erythema, no arm swelling. No edema. No peripheral stigmata.

A/P
1. Enterococcal tricuspid IE - on track. Weekly labs going to us and ID. ID visit end of January, TTE after.
2. HTN - fine, continue.
3. BPH with chronic retention - stable; urology in spring.
Text line for anything. Return in about 6 weeks after therapy ends.
